proposition: In his late twenties, at his brother's insistence, Ibn Turka set out on some fifteen years of study abroad (roughly 795-810/1393-1408, both dates marked 'c.' in the timeline), because, by his account, circumstances in Iran were too strait to carry on the family legacy in philosophy and mystical theory.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I (829/1426), addressed to Shāhrukh
mediation.note: the reason given is his own

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, Nafsat al-Maṣdūr II (1431-32), addressed to Bāysunghur
mediation.note: written to seek intercession from the ruler's son while his case was still unresolved
'late twenties' is MK's; the timeline dates are approximate
